Subject: Unexpected truncation when streaming / SDK vs Hosted API

Hi Hannah —

Quick heads-up from our testing: when we switch to the Python SDK streaming client (v0.9.2) for our multi-turn patient summary workflow, responses are intermittently truncated mid-sentence. The same request executed directly against the hosted REST endpoint returns a full response every time. We tried toggling max_tokens and setting chunk_size to 1, but the truncated responses look like a KV-cache mismatch (earlier tokens missing in later decoding steps).

I attached a trimmed log and a tiny repro script that reproduces the issue for us. This is impacting our weekend canary. Could you loop in runtime if this looks like an SDK->runtime compatibility problem?

Thanks,
Beth
Beth Green

Thanks Hannah / Beth — I pulled the attached logs. A few preliminary observations:

- The HAR trace (api_call_trace.har) shows the chunked response arrives to the SDK, but the SDK client appears to stop consuming after the third chunk in reproducible runs. The runtime subsequently emits a warning about KV cache eviction for that sequence id.
- On our side the kernel logs show a cache compaction event at about the same token index. If the SDK client drops the connection or fails to ACK some stream frame, the runtime may be pruning KV entries prematurely and the decode resumes with a partial cache.

Repro plan (I can run tomorrow on a dev cluster):
1) Run the repro script with SDK v0.9.2 and capture tcpdump of the streaming socket.
2) Re-run using raw REST streaming curl and compare chunk boundaries and content.
3) Instrument the runtime to keep TLS socket alive and disable KV compaction for that run to see if truncation goes away.

Ask: can the Acme SRE team share whether they are using any proxy between their client and our endpoint (nginx, envoy)? Proxies with aggressive timeouts or connection drain could cause the SDK to see a truncated stream.

Karthik
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
